_meta.method: pure config/code reading + arithmetic on existing .sol results, no new solves

S1_capital_costs.annuity_formula: ANF(i,n) = i*(1+i)^n / ((1+i)^n - 1), identical for all technologies and both networks

fixed_om_cost.note: ComponentInvestmentConfig/StorageInvestmentConfig dataclasses in investment_calculator.py have no O&M field. opex_fixed_eur_per_mw_yr exists only in calion/config/schemas/tech_library_schema.py, an unused schema for a different config pathway. No technology (HP, EK, TES, existing CHP/boilers) carries a fixed O&M cost anywhere in the objective for this project.

heat_pump.source_comment: Pieper, Ommen, Buehler, Lava Paaske, Elmegaard & Markussen, 'Allocation of investment costs for large-scale heat pumps supplying district heating', Energy Procedia 147 (2018) 358-367; 26 real Danish DH-HP installations, 0.8-1.1 M EUR/MW (2017 data). Harmonized 2026-07-20 (was 400k, undocumented asymmetry).

electric_boiler.source_comment: Danish Energy Agency Technology Catalogue (efficiency reference; CAPEX source not explicitly cited in config comment)
electric_boiler.deviation_note: config uses 25y vs. 20y literature expectation, 5y above, not flagged as an issue elsewhere

thermal_storage.cost_model: degressive per-tank power law, see S2
thermal_storage.source_comment: engineering estimate (ASME thin-wall pressure vessel sizing), explicitly NOT a vendor quote

existing_chp_boilers.note: existing infrastructure, no capital cost in the objective at all -- intentional greenfield-decision framing, but a real asymmetry vs. investable assets

S2_tes_cost_curve.formula: C(V) = N * c0 * (V/N / v0)^b, evaluated per-tank at N=ceil(V/unit_tank_m3) identical tanks

parameters_shared_both_networks.source: configs/paper_2/storage_geometry.yaml top-level defaults, inherited by both tes_sb and tes_main (neither per_asset block overrides these fields)

unit_tank_m3.source: network-specific asset block in Stadtbach_topo.yaml / Memmingen_P2_base.yaml

S2_tes_cost_curve.saturation_note: EUR/m3 flattens at exactly unit_tank_m3 (5000 m3) -- degression benefit caps at single-tank scale, larger volumes just add identical tanks at the same per-m3 rate

validity_range_check.inconsistency: both networks' actual V_min_m3 sit below the config's own documented realism floor of 50 m3

MM.concrete_case: Q3's c0x0.5 run built exactly a 1.1 MWh (~76 m3) tank -- in this questionable-validity zone, not hypothetical

validity_range_check.conclusion: MM's small-tank ladder rungs are extrapolated well outside the cost curve's likely validated range (~1000 m3); SB's ladder stays safely above it. Reported only, no change made -- ladder truncation or a second small-buffer cost dataset is the author's decision.

S3_prices.electricity_sell_price_formula: max(strompreis_EUR_MWh[t] - sell_spread(0), sell_floor(0)) * (1 - sell_haircut(0)) - sell_fee(0) + sell_premium(0) = raw spot price, unmodified
S3_prices.gap_components_per_config_comment: MS Arbeitspreis + KWKG 0.446 + Offshore 0.941 + BesAR/§19 0.05 + Konzessionsabgabe 0.11 + Stromsteuer 0.05 ct/kWh
S3_prices.asymmetry_note: sell_haircut/sell_spread/sell_fee mechanisms exist in code but are 0 in both network configs -- CHP electricity sale is modeled at the full raw wholesale price with zero marketing/balancing discount, an unquantified optimistic simplification for the generation side
S3_prices.harmonization: gridcost_eur_mwh and all fuel prices harmonized between SB and MM on 2026-07-29 (previously undocumented asymmetries)

price_timeseries_stats.status: not computed in this audit pass (time budget) -- mean/min/max/stddev of strompreis_EUR_MWh for 2025 not pulled

S4_demand_charge.reference_quantity: single annual peak of grid electricity import (P_buy), hourly resolution (dt_h=1h), no monthly-peak mechanism found
S4_demand_charge.triggering_assets: any asset drawing grid electricity at the coincident peak hour -- for SB effectively hp_sb/ek_sb only (CHP/boilers generate electricity, they don't import it)

base_vs_wp_point_comparison_sb_eur.note: the forced HP point's demand charge is ~7x BASE -- the 5.33 MW HP creates a new, much higher import peak

biomass_is_zero_check.note: biomass EF is 20 kg/MWh, not 0 -- likely lifecycle/harvest/transport emissions, not combustion CO2; not further documented in code why exactly 20

S5_co2_emissions.grid_co2_mechanism: hourly grid_co2_kg_MWh timeseries (electricitymaps) used in both objective and reporting -- the static ef_el_kg_per_mwh=400 field is explicitly marked UNUSED in the config comment

gross_net_double_counting_check.model_optimizes: gross (CHP electricity emissions, no self-use netting)
gross_net_double_counting_check.reconciliation: the netting difference appears explicitly and labeled as CO2_selfuse_netting_adjustment_EUR in every cost_breakdown.json (e.g. SB-S0-HK0-PIN0: -1,606,644.23 EUR historically / current run -1,585,028.80 EUR aux total dominated by this term) -- it is a KPI attribution correction only, does not double-count into the real objective cost (real_costs_EUR.CO2_cost_EUR stays gross)

objective_revenue_terms: P_sell[t] * sell_price[t] (CHP electricity sale, reported as Grid_sell_revenue_EUR, negative sign)

eeg_kwkg_subsidy_check.verification: no import/call in system_builder.py, model_finalizer.py, or cost_calculator.py -- report-only, confirmed dead for optimization purposes
eeg_kwkg_subsidy_check.real_world_gap: a real biomass CHP plant of this size (14.5 MW) would typically receive an EEG/KWKG feed-in premium above the wholesale price under German law -- this potential extra revenue is absent from the model
eeg_kwkg_subsidy_check.action: reported only, not implemented, per instruction

base_years.hp_ek_capex_literature: 2017-2018 (Pieper et al.), no visible inflation adjustment

S7_consistency.om_asymmetry: none between technologies -- structurally absent for ALL technologies (see S1), not a single-technology gap
S7_consistency.tac_formula: TAC = sum(CAPEX_annualized) + sum(Activation_annualized) + Fuel_cost + Grid_energy_cost + Grid_sell_revenue(negative) + CO2_cost + Demand_charge_cost [=real_costs_total_EUR] + aux_terms(Dump/TieBreaker/StorageInstall/Terminal/DemandSlack/ReturnAnchor/PressureReg/LateralTiebreak/PressureSlack/DataClosureEpsilon/CO2SelfuseNetting) [=model_aux_terms_total_EUR] + residual = objective_total_EUR (from Gurobi)
S7_consistency.reconciliation_check_status: OK, confirmed structurally for every run checked this session, not just this one

_meta.purpose: V2d(a)/V2e(a-b) mandatory source table for TES cost-curve plausibility check (docs SS4bu). Supersedes the S2 eur_per_m3_table above, which predates V2/V2b/V2c/V2d/V2e's unit_tank_m3 changes and is kept only as a historical S1-S7-audit snapshot.
_meta.root_cause_corrected: an earlier '93 EUR/m3 at 6,000 m3' citation (SS4bt(c)) was found NOT to exist anywhere in the cited source after reading the actual paper full-text; it was an artifact of an AI WebSearch summary, never verified against the primary document. See SS4bu(a) for the full incident and the resulting rule: cite only from a read primary document or a structured API, never a web-summary alone.

primary_source.citation: Luechinger, R., Hendry, R., Walter, H., Worlitschek, J., Schuetz, P. (2025). 'Cost Analysis for Large Thermal Energy Storage Systems.' ASME J. Eng. Sustain. Bldgs. Cities, 6(2):021006. DOI 10.1115/1.4069122. CC-BY 4.0.
primary_source.verification_method: full 14-page PDF (incl. Appendix A-F) read directly via file-read tool, not WebFetch AI-summarization
primary_source.cost_data_scope: paper defines its figures only as 'investment costs' / 'capital costs' from desk research on published projects; no explicit turnkey vs. bare-vessel definition given. Indirect scope evidence (p.3): 'In Mannheim, 26% of the cost was allocated to the tank, including the foundation, internal structures, and insulation. In Flensburg, this proportion was 56%' -- implies total project cost is broader than the vessel alone (foundation+structure+insulation+unnamed other cost blocks, plausibly connection/planning); land/site acquisition is never explicitly mentioned as included or excluded.
primary_source.price_basis_in_paper: PPP-adjusted and inflation-adjusted to 2023 price level, reported per-country in CHF/GBP/USD/EUR

inflation_index.source: Eurostat API dataset sts_inpp_m (Producer prices in industry, domestic market, monthly)
inflation_index.series: geo=DE, nace_r2=C25 (Manufacture of fabricated metal products, except machinery and equipment), unit=I21 (index 2021=100), s_adj=NSA
inflation_index.retrieval_method: direct Eurostat REST JSON API call, raw values read (not AI-summarized)

currency_and_inflation_adjustment_to_202.note: first attempt used a Destatis page via WebFetch AI-summary, which returned an internally inconsistent figure (~flat 2023->2026 despite a stated +4.6% YoY) and was discarded in favor of the direct Eurostat API pull -- second occurrence of the same WebFetch-summary failure mode in this pass, see SS4bu(a).

appendix_d_named_atmospheric_ttes_projec.outlier_hypothesis_unverified: inner-city Berlin siting / constrained footprint / ancillary-facility cost, not confirmed against the paper's cited input source (saisonalspeicher.de) in this pass

conclusion.finding: model curve is at or below every named real project at matched volume, never above -- the earlier 'model overprices storage 3.1x' finding is retracted as unfounded (based on a non-existent citation)
conclusion.reuter_west_status: remains a SIZE reference only (justifies max_tank_m3=50,000), explicitly NOT used as a cost anchor
